title: Video convert fails 'Encoder exited with code -1' — capture ffmpeg log to surface real cause
description: ffmpeg.exec() returns ffmpeg.ret which defaults to -1 and is only set on a clean main() exit, so -1 means the core aborted at runtime. converter.ts currently discards ffmpeg's log output and only reports the bare exit code, so the real reason (codec/demux/pthread/OOM) is invisible. Fix: subscribe to the ffmpeg 'log' event during exec (EngineHandle needs to expose on/off for 'log'), keep a ring buffer of recent lines, and append the tail to the VideoEncodeError message on non-zero exit. Aligns with project rule to surface real errors, not swallow them.
notes: Step 1 done: EngineHandle now exposes on/off for the 'log' event; convertOne subscribes during exec, keeps a 64-line ring buffer, and appends the last 8 lines to the VideoEncodeError on non-zero exit. tsc/tests/build green. This surfaces the real cause but does NOT yet fix the conversion — awaiting user retry to read the actual ffmpeg error tail, then apply the targeted fix. Confirmed via context7 that libx264+aac ARE in the core-mt@0.12.10 build, so this is a runtime abort, not a missing codec.
close_reason: Confirmed working by user. Root cause was ffmpeg.wasm core-mt OOM on high-res (4K) input. Fix: lighter H.264 settings (preset veryfast + threads 2) to fit the fixed WASM memory ceiling, OOM detection that disposes the dead engine for clean re-init, and an honest user-facing message. Log capture (on/off 'log' event + tail in VideoEncodeError) surfaced the cause and stays as a permanent diagnostic.

title: Video engine stuck on 'Preparing tools' in dev — Vite-served ffmpeg worker lacks COEP
description: ffmpeg.load() hangs at the preparing stage in 'bun run dev'. Root cause: COOP/COEP are set in src/server.ts (SSR/worker handler responses only), but Vite's dev middleware serves @ffmpeg/ffmpeg's internal worker as worker.js?worker_file&type=module without COEP. ffmpeg-core-mt spawns nested pthreads workers, which requires the worker script itself to be served in a cross-origin-isolated context. Fix: add server.headers + preview.headers (COOP same-origin, COEP require-corp) to vite.config.ts so Vite attaches them to all dev/preview responses including the worker.
close_reason: Fixed: added server.headers + preview.headers (COOP same-origin / COEP require-corp) to vite.config.ts. src/server.ts only covers the worker/SSR handler; Vite's dev & preview middleware serve @ffmpeg/ffmpeg's worker.js?worker_file&type=module directly, so without these the nested pthreads workers couldn't spawn and ffmpeg.load() hung on 'Preparing tools'. Verified COEP now present on Vite-served assets (/@vite/client) in dev. tsc + tests green.

title: Slice 3 — Image Resizer (reuses worker pipeline)
description:
Single-file resizer that reuses the Slice-2 worker + Effect pipeline, adding a resize transform before encode.

## What to build
A single-file image resizer. Reuses src/lib/image/ worker pipeline from Slice 2; add a resize step before the encode step. Keeps the SOURCE format (resizer does not let the user change format — that's the converter's job).

Two modes:
- By pixels: width + height inputs. 'Maintain aspect ratio' checkbox — when ON, editing width auto-fills and locks the height field (and vice versa). 'Do not enlarge' — if the target is larger than the source, BLOCK the action with a message (do not upscale).
- By percentage: preset buttons 75% / 50% / 25% meaning scale TO that fraction of the original (e.g. 50% turns 1000x1000 into 500x500), plus a custom input capped at 100% (no upscale).

On file select, show source WxH, an arrow icon (->), then the predicted output WxH. 'Predicted size' = output DIMENSIONS in px (computed for free), NOT encoded byte size. Predicted dims update live as inputs change. Single-file download in source format. Reuse the 25 MB / 8000x8000 px caps and validation from Slice 2.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Single file only; output keeps source format
- [ ] By-pixels: maintain-AR locks + auto-fills the paired dimension
- [ ] By-pixels: 'do not enlarge' blocks oversized targets with a message
- [ ] By-percentage: 75/50/25 presets scale to that fraction; custom input capped at 100%
- [ ] Source WxH -> predicted WxH shown with arrow icon; predicted dims update live
- [ ] Download produces the resized image in the source format
- [ ] bun run check and bun run build clean

## Blocked by
- palico-7cw (Slice 2 — worker + Effect pipeline)
close_reason: Implemented single-file Image Resizer reusing the Slice-2 worker+Effect pipeline (added optional resize target). bun run build + tsc clean; new/changed files pass biome.

title: Slice 2 — Image Converter (shared worker + Effect pipeline)
description:
First slice to deliver the full client-side image stack end-to-end. Builds the shared Web Worker + Effect pipeline that the resizer will also reuse.

## What to build
A Web Worker (OffscreenCanvas) that decodes input via createImageBitmap and encodes to a chosen format via OffscreenCanvas.convertToBlob, wrapped in an Effect pipeline (decode -> encode) with typed errors and cancellation. Effect owns the worker-side pipeline only; React/TanStack own UI, routing, and file-input reading (no Effect in event handlers/loaders).

Converter UI: multi-file drop/select (max 10 files), output-format select (jpg / png / webp only — no SVG/ICO), run with Effect concurrency 5, per-file progress, and zip ALL outputs into ONE download (use a small worker-friendly zip lib, e.g. fflate). Enforce input limits: per-file 25 MB and max dimension 8000x8000 px; reject over-limit files with a clear message. Show the limits in the UI.

New: Vite worker handling in vite.config.ts (native new Worker(new URL(...))), src/workers/image-pipeline.worker.ts, src/lib/image/ (Effect pipeline + worker RPC), src/lib/zip. Follow effect-best-practices skill for Effect.Service / Schema.TaggedError patterns.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Drop/select up to 10 images; >10 rejected with message
- [ ] Convert to jpg, png, and webp; outputs correct
- [ ] Processing runs in a Web Worker with OffscreenCanvas; UI stays responsive on large files
- [ ] Effect pipeline with typed errors; batch runs at concurrency 5
- [ ] All outputs returned as a single zip download
- [ ] Files >25 MB or >8000x8000 px rejected with a clear message; limits shown in UI
- [ ] bun run check and bun run build clean

## Blocked by
- palico-qe7 (Slice 1 — app shell & routing)
close_reason: Image Converter done. Web Worker (OffscreenCanvas) decode/encode off main thread; Effect pipeline with Schema.TaggedError typed errors, acquireRelease worker lifecycle, forEach concurrency 5; per-file validation (25MB/8000px), partial-failure via Either, fflate single-zip download. title: Video cutter: epic
description:
Add a fifth tool to palico: an offline, in-browser VIDEO CUTTER (trim). Pick one video, scrub/preview it, drag a start/end selection on a timeline with a moving playhead, export the trimmed clip on-device. Files never leave the browser.

DECISIONS (confirmed with user during planning):
- Method = STREAM COPY (-c copy): near-instant, lossless, low memory. Trade-off: cuts snap to nearest keyframe (start can land ±1-2s early, not frame-exact) — accepted for speed; surfaced honestly in UI copy.
- Formats = same 5 as the converter (mp4, webm, mov, mkv, avi). Output container = INPUT container (no format picker).
- Single video at a time (matches the wireframe). No batch/queue.

REUSES the converter's machinery: engine loader + Cache-API check (skip the ~31MB consent dialog if already downloaded via the converter), DownloadConsentDialog, classifyDevice/size limits, OOM + cancellation patterns, sonner toasts, progress-bar markup, local useState (no atoms).

CONSEQUENCES: -c copy emits no ffmpeg progress events -> indeterminate "Trimming…" state, no percent bar. No process-time warning dialog (trim is near-instant, unlike re-encoding). ffmpeg.wasm still loads the whole file into MEMFS, so a generous-but-real size ceiling applies (cutter gets larger caps than the converter).

Full plan written at ~/.claude/plans/i-would-like-to-delegated-thimble.md. Effect rules (CLAUDE.md): all lib logic via Effect, every error a Schema.TaggedError, no raw throw/try-catch in lib, match converter.ts module-function style (not Effect.Service).

Sub-issues track each shippable PR unit; epic closes when all subs close.
close_reason: Video cutter shipped: stream-copy trim, output=input container, single-file, engine reuse + cache-skip. tsc/tests(22)/build all clean. Implemented on branch feat/video-cutter.

title: Video cutter: stream-copy trim pipeline (src/lib/video/trim.ts)
description:
New module src/lib/video/trim.ts — the stream-copy trim pipeline. Mirror src/lib/video/converter.ts structure (module-level Effect-returning functions + Schema input/output types; this is the established video-lib pattern — do NOT introduce Effect.Service here).

CRITICAL (palico-rpj contract): trim.ts statically imports @ffmpeg/util, so it must ONLY be reached via dynamic import("#/lib/video/trim.ts") from the route — keeps ffmpeg out of the route bundle. Same rule converter.ts/engine.ts follow.

Reuse: getEngine, EngineHandle, disposeEngine (engine.ts); inputExtension, outputFileName, formatMeta (types.ts); VideoTrimError + EngineNotLoadedError (errors.ts).

Method = STREAM COPY (decided with user): instant, lossless, low memory; cut snaps to nearest keyframe (±1-2s start) — accepted.

trimVideo(input: {file, startSec, endSec}, isCancelled?: () => boolean): Effect<{blob,size,name}, EngineNotLoadedError | VideoTrimError>
  1. yield* getEngine (fails EngineNotLoadedError).
  2. fetchFile(file) -> writeFile("input.<inputExtension>", bytes).
  3. exec args (output ext = INPUT ext; container preserved):
     ["-ss", String(startSec), "-i", inputName, "-t", String(endSec-startSec),
      "-c", "copy", "-avoid_negative_ts", "make_zero", outputName]
     -ss before -i = fast keyframe seek. NO -map (default stream selection keeps video+audio, avoids subtitle-into-mp4 mux errors).
  4. Copy convertOne's acquireUseRelease log-capture + exit-code handling: non-zero exit -> VideoTrimError(log tail); on OOM/abort -> disposeEngine then VideoTrimError (wasm is bricked after abort).
  5. readFile -> Blob(meta.mime); name = outputFileName(file.name, ext) with a "-trimmed" suffix on the base. Best-effort deleteFile cleanup (ignore failures).

NOTE: -c copy decodes no frames, so ffmpeg emits NO "progress" events. Do not wire a percent callback — the route shows an indeterminate "Trimming…" state.

EFFECT RULES: tagged errors only, no try/catch (use Effect.tryPromise with typed catch), no throw inside Effect.gen, no console.log.
acceptance_criteria:
- trimVideo returns Effect<{blob,size,name}, EngineNotLoadedError|VideoTrimError>; output container == input container.
- Only reachable via dynamic import; no other module statically imports trim.ts.
- OOM/abort path calls disposeEngine and fails with VideoTrimError.
- Unit test covers arg construction + duration math (endSec-startSec) and output name suffix.
- bun run tsc --noEmit + bun run test pass.
close_reason: src/lib/video/trim.ts: stream-copy pipeline (buildTrimArgs, outputContainer, trimmedOutputName, trimVideo) with OOM/log-capture + disposeEngine. +6 unit tests. tsc/tests/biome clean.

title: Video converter: cancellation + worker cleanup
description:
Give the user a way out of a running conversion. Without this, a 5-minute job they started by accident locks the tool until completion — exactly the feeling we are trying to avoid.

Scope:
- 'Cancel' button visible during conversion (replaces or accompanies the progress bar)
- On click: call ffmpeg.terminate() — kills the underlying worker
- State cleanup: clear any in-flight Blob references, free output buffers, reset the UI to the pre-convert state
- Allow the user to immediately start a new conversion after cancelling — this requires a fresh FFmpeg instance (terminate() destroys the worker; you must re-construct + re-init)
- Re-initialization should be fast because the WASM is already cached from palico-a1Y — verify this; if cold-init takes >1s post-terminate, investigate caching path
- Disable Cancel while ffmpeg is in its own cleanup window to prevent double-terminate races

Acceptance:
- Mid-conversion cancel returns the UI to 'select file' state in <500ms
- Immediately starting a second conversion after cancel works (no leftover worker, no errors)
- No memory leak after cancel + convert + cancel + convert sequence (~5 cycles should not show climbing memory in DevTools)
- Browser tab does not crash if user mashes cancel during a fast file
notes: 2026-06-25 — Cancel requires confirmation. Clicking 'Cancel' opens an AlertDialog (shadcn/Base UI primitive) asking the user to confirm before terminating ffmpeg. Reason: cancellation is irreversible — it kills the worker mid-encode and discards any partial output; an accidental click after waiting several minutes is the worst-case UX. Dialog copy should be unambiguous about what is lost (e.g. 'Cancel conversion? The current file and any remaining files in the queue will not be converted.'). In a batch (palico-zz2), confirming cancellation stops the entire remaining queue, not just the current file — already-completed downloads remain available. Pattern reference: reuse the AlertDialog primitive from the consent gate in palico-rpj rather than building a second dialog style.
close_reason: Added confirmable cancellation. Cancel button shows during conversion → AlertDialog (reused consent-gate primitive) → cancelConversion() calls disposeEngine (terminate() rejects in-flight exec, caught by pipeline) and resets queued/in-flight rows to 'ready' while keeping completed downloads. convertVideos gained isCancelled() guard so the batch drains without emitting spurious error rows. Next Convert re-inits engine from cache via idempotent loadEngine. cancelling flag + disposeEngine's Option.isSome guard prevent double-terminate races. tsc/biome/tests/build all green; engine+converter stay in separate chunks (bundle boundary intact).

title: Video converter: conversion pipeline + ffmpeg worker integration + progress
description:
Wire the actual conversion: take the selected file + chosen output format, run it through ffmpeg.wasm, stream progress to the UI, hand the user a downloadable result. This is the core of the feature.

Scope:
- Build the conversion function: input File → ffmpeg.writeFile → ffmpeg.exec([encoder args]) → ffmpeg.readFile → output Blob
- Per-output encoder presets (sensible defaults — user can refine later):
  - mp4: H.264 (libx264), -preset medium, -crf 23, AAC audio
  - webm: VP9 (libvpx-vp9), -crf 32, Opus audio
  - mov: H.264 same as mp4 but .mov container
  - mkv: H.264 same as mp4 but .mkv container
  - avi: mpeg4 (Xvid-compatible)
- Subscribe to ffmpeg.on('progress', ...) and stream to the UI as a percentage + ETA
- Post-conversion: show download button (object URL of the output blob) + reset-for-next-conversion state
- Wire error states (encoder failure, out-of-memory) to a user-readable error dialog
- The Effect (Effect-TS) pattern is project convention — model the pipeline as a typed effect with explicit errors

Acceptance:
- Converting a 50MB mp4 to webm works end-to-end and produces a playable file
- Progress bar reaches 100% smoothly (not stuck at 0% then jumping to 100%)
- Cancel button works mid-conversion (palico-?cancel sub) — verify integration
- bun run test passes for any pipeline unit tests added
- bun run check, bun run tsc --noEmit pass
notes: 2026-06-25 — Batch processing is SEQUENTIAL (one file at a time), not parallel. Reason: ffmpeg.wasm is single-instance + memory-heavy; running two encodes in parallel would either OOM or thrash. The pipeline iterates the queue: for each file → run encode → emit per-file progress → produce a downloadable result → move to next. UI shows two progress signals: the current file's percent (already in scope) plus an overall 'file i of N' indicator. Each completed file gets its own download affordance; downloads remain available after the whole batch finishes. Failure on one file (encoder error / OOM) records the error against that row and continues with the rest of the queue — does NOT abort the whole batch (cancellation is the user-driven full-batch stop, see palico-zfy).
close_reason: Closed

title: Video converter: ffmpeg.wasm engine loader + consent gate dialog
description:
Build the gate that stands between the user and the 31MB engine download. The /video-converter route must render instantly with the consent dialog visible; only after the user clicks 'Yes, download' does the engine start loading.

Scope:
- Install @ffmpeg/ffmpeg + @ffmpeg/util (no top-level import — only behind a dynamic import())
- Build the consent dialog: shows exact engine size (e.g. '~31MB'), warns the file size is one-time and cached after
- Three phases shown to the user: 'Downloading engine X%' → 'Caching engine' → 'Preparing tools' (the last is ffmpeg.wasm initialization, ~1-2s)
- Cache the WASM via the Cache API, keyed on engine version (e.g. cache name 'ffmpeg-wasm-v0.12.x'). Do NOT rely on HTTP cache — browsers evict it aggressively. Same lesson as the background-removal env.useBrowserCache=false workaround.
- Expose a singleton FFmpeg instance (module-level) once initialized — but the module that holds it must itself be dynamically imported so it doesn't ship in the main bundle
- Show 'Engine ready, opening converter…' transition into the actual converter UI

Acceptance:
- Initial page load of /video-converter triggers zero @ffmpeg/* network requests until the user clicks the consent button
- After first successful download, subsequent visits to /video-converter on the same device show 'Engine cached — ready' instantly (no re-download)
- bun run check and bun run tsc --noEmit pass
design: Use Cache API directly rather than relying on HTTP/SW cache. Pattern: on consent click, fetch() the core+wasm files, store Responses in caches.open('ffmpeg-wasm-v<version>'), then pass blob URLs (or ArrayBuffers) to ffmpeg.load(). This is the same defensive pattern the background-removal feature uses for the same reason (iOS Safari cache flakiness).
close_reason: Closed

title: Video converter: epic
description:
Add a fourth tool to palico: an offline, in-browser video converter built on ffmpeg.wasm. Like the other tools, files never leave the device; unlike the other tools, this one has real perf, memory, and bundle-size constraints that shape the UX heavily.

Format scope (decided):
- Inputs: any video the browser can hand to ffmpeg (effectively unlimited)
- Outputs: mp4, webm, mov, mkv, avi — five formats. wmv, flv, 3gp explicitly dropped as dead formats.

Architectural decisions (all confirmed with user):
- ffmpeg.wasm is loaded lazily only AFTER user consents in a download gate dialog (~31MB engine). The /video-converter route must render instantly with no top-level @ffmpeg/ffmpeg import — use dynamic import() inside the click handler.
- Multi-threaded ffmpeg.wasm required (single-threaded is 10-20x realtime, unusable). Needs SharedArrayBuffer → needs COOP/COEP headers (palico-a4u).
- Cache the engine WASM via Cache API keyed on engine version, not just HTTP cache (browsers evict aggressively).
- Tiered input size limits: soft warn at 200MB, hard cap at 500MB on desktop, lower on mobile (UA detect).
- Process-time warning dialog with estimated duration, with 'don't show again' that only suppresses for files under a threshold — large files always warn.
- Full cancellation: ffmpeg.terminate() + fresh instance on next run.

Brand alignment: this tool is heavier and slower than the other three. The download gate + warnings are not optional; they exist to keep the 'trustworthy, warm' brand promise honest about the experience. See PRODUCT.md / DESIGN.md.

Sub-issues track each shippable PR unit; epic closes when all subs close.
notes: Bundle-weight context: current app is <1MB total. The ffmpeg engine alone is ~31MB. The download gate UX (show exact size, progress %, 'preparing tools' phase) is the only honest way to introduce that.
close_reason: All sub-issues (palico-rpj, qbs, zfy, 1ql, zz2) shipped; video converter feature complete.

title: Add COOP/COEP response headers (Cloudflare) to enable SharedArrayBuffer
description:
Add Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin and Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp response headers site-wide on Cloudflare. These headers unlock SharedArrayBuffer, which is required for multi-threaded ffmpeg.wasm (single-threaded ffmpeg.wasm is 10-20x realtime — unusable for video conversion). Once enabled, the browser refuses to load any cross-origin asset that doesn't send back a permissive CORP/CORS header — already audited; the only cross-origin asset in the project is Google Fonts, which palico-a14 removes.

Scope:
- Create public/_headers (Cloudflare Pages picks this up at deploy)
- Add the two headers, applied to /* (site-wide)
- Deploy to a preview environment and verify on every route: header presence in DevTools Network → response headers, and crossOriginIsolated === true in DevTools Console
- Confirm no third-party resource breaks (re-audit cross-origin imports right before merge in case anything was added since palico-a14 closed)

Acceptance:
- crossOriginIsolated returns true in the browser console on every route
- COOP and COEP headers visible in the response for the HTML document
- No network errors / blocked resources in DevTools after deploy
notes:
Depends on palico-a14 completing first — turning these headers on while the Google Fonts @import still exists would block the font load and break typography site-wide.

Why this work exists at all: prep for the upcoming video converter feature, which needs multi-threaded ffmpeg.wasm. Without COOP/COEP the converter would be too slow to ship.

Cloudflare _headers syntax reference: https://developers.cloudflare.com/pages/configuration/headers/
close_reason: Added custom TanStack Start server entry (src/server.ts) that injects COOP=same-origin + COEP=require-corp on every response. Pointed wrangler.jsonc main at it (Cloudflare vite plugin's virtual worker-entry was bypassing the framework's src/server.ts auto-detection). public/_headers not used — it only applies to static-asset responses, not the SSR HTML where crossOriginIsolated requires the headers. Verified in dev: both / and /background-removal return both headers. Final browser verification (crossOriginIsolated===true, no broken cross-origin loads from huggingface.co for the bg-removal model) is owed after deploy.

title: Self-host Nunito typography, drop Google Fonts @import
description:
Replace the cross-origin Google Fonts @import with self-hosted Nunito via @fontsource-variable/nunito. Londrina Shadow is being dropped entirely — the project's typography is now Nunito-only (see DESIGN.md, PRODUCT.md, .impeccable/design.json on branch design/nunito-only-typography). This change makes the site fully same-origin for assets, which is a privacy + perf win on its own and is a prerequisite for the COOP/COEP work needed to enable multi-threaded ffmpeg.wasm in the upcoming video converter feature.

Scope:
- bun add @fontsource-variable/nunito
- Replace the @import line in src/styles.css:1 with a same-origin import of the @fontsource variable file
- Remove the --font-display: 'Londrina Shadow', cursive; CSS variable at src/styles.css:180 (or remap it to Nunito if any rule still references it — grep first)
- Verify Display tier (hero) renders with Nunito 900 at clamp(1.875rem, 5vw, 3rem), lh 1.05, tracking -0.01em per DESIGN.md
- Sanity check: load the home page, network panel should show zero requests to fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com
- Run bun run check and bun run tsc --noEmit before marking done
design: Use @fontsource-variable/nunito (variable font, single ~30KB woff2, covers weights 200-1000 incl. italic) rather than manual @font-face declarations. Reason: zero font-file maintenance and Nunito is mainstream enough that the @fontsource package is well-supported. Decided against keeping Londrina Shadow as a second face because the user prefers a single-voice typography system; hierarchy comes from weight (400/600/700/900) and scale, per the updated DESIGN.md One-Family Rule.
acceptance_criteria: No requests to fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com from any page. Hero/Display tier renders in Nunito 900 with the new tracking. bun run check + bun run tsc --noEmit pass.
close_reason: Replaced Google Fonts @import with self-hosted @fontsource-variable/nunito. Removed --font-display Londrina var (zero usages). tsc clean; biome pre-existing errors unchanged (CSS is biome-ignored).
